links.comparator_used: Prompt with no audience, tone or reading-level specification (no additional context)
links.outcome: Readability of LLM responses to male infertility FAQs (Flesch Reading Ease and SMOG)
links.effect: Readability improved across all five models after contextual prompting; e.g., Grok mean FRE 69.71±6.09 and SMOG 9.96±1.04 after prompting, versus non-prompted DeepSeek FRE 46.28±6.86 and SMOG 11.71±0.76 and Claude FRE 23.83±12.29 and SMOG 16.37±2.47
links.tradeoff: Accuracy was not assessed; the authors state readability gains must be paired with ongoing verification of clinical accuracy to mitigate misinformation risk.
links.quote: These findings suggest that simple contextual prompting can substantially enhance readability of LLM-generated male infertility education; however, readability gains must be paired with ongoing verification of clinical accuracy to mitigate misinformation risk.

links.comparator_used: Default prompt with no reading-level or audience instruction (no additional context)
links.outcome: Readability of patient-facing LLM output (FRE and SMOG)
links.effect: Readability improved across all models with a lay patient/couple audience prompt; Grok after prompting FRE 69.71±6.09, SMOG 9.96±1.04
links.tradeoff: Clinical accuracy was not evaluated; the authors state readability gains must be paired with ongoing verification of accuracy.
links.quote: After prompting, Grok generated the most readable responses (mean FRE 69.71±6.09; mean SMOG 9.96±1.04), and readability improved across all models.

design_hint: contextual prompting for lay reading level
